title: The Cisco CLI Modes: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Think of an office building with security. Each floor needs a higher pass. I O S modes work the same way.

lines.t: Floors you need a pass for
IOS modes work the same way

scenes.heading: The security levels
scenes.narration: You climb through the modes one at a time. User mode ends with a greater than sign, and only allows basic checks. Type enable to reach privileged mode, which ends with a hash. Configure terminal takes you to global configuration. From there, you enter interface or line modes.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. You must enable first. Exit goes back one level. Enable secret takes priority.

items.wrong: Config mode straight from user mode
Password and secret are the same

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva the CLI lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Greater than is user mode, and hash is privileged. Configure terminal enters global config. Exit goes back one level. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva the CLI lab.
